Ridu 0.7.0 types virtual fields by their resolver and adds Payload's rich-text toolbar and layout options. A computed display name now returns a plain Go string: `operation.Present(first + " " + last)` replaces a separate value-type argument and a `store.String` wrapper, and the compiler checks the type. The CMS still builds into one Go binary with its static admin embedded.

## Try Ridu

Install Go 1.25.13 or newer, Node.js 24 and Bun 1.4.0, then run:

```sh
bun create ridu@0.7.0 my-ridu-app
cd my-ridu-app
bun install
bun run dev
```

Choose SQLite for a local trial without a separate database service. See the [quickstart](https://riducms.com/docs/quickstart/) and [deployment guide](https://riducms.com/docs/production/).

## What changed

- `field.Virtual(name, resolver)` takes its value type from the resolver: `operation.Value[string]`, `operation.Value[float64]`, `operation.Value[bool]`, or `operation.Value[store.Value]` for any JSON value. `.AfterRead` transforms use the same type.
- A scalar resolver can no longer return the wrong kind; that mistake is now a compile error instead of an `invalid_computed_value` failure at run time.
- `richtext.Config.Admin` changes how a rich-text editor looks in the admin, matching Payload's editor options: `FixedToolbar` pins formatting controls above the editor, `HideGutter` removes the edge line and indent, and `HideDraggableBlockElement`, `HideAddBlockButton`, and `HideInsertParagraphAtEnd` hide block controls. The floating toolbar over selected text is unchanged.
- An upload field shows a cropped preview of its image and a readable size such as "95 kB".
- The breadcrumb shows a document's full title when the header has room.
- The rich-text documentation is split into pages for features, toolbar and layout, custom blocks, and display.

## Breaking changes and upgrading from 0.6.x

Run the new CLI's upgrade command from the project root, then review and commit the result:

```sh
bunx @riducms/cli@0.7.0 upgrade 0.7.0
```

Update each virtual field:

```go
// Before
field.Virtual("displayName", field.ValueString,
	func(ctx operation.Context) (operation.Value[store.Value], error) {
		return operation.Present(store.String(name)), nil
	})

// After
field.Virtual("displayName",
	func(ctx operation.Context) (operation.Value[string], error) {
		return operation.Present(name), nil
	})
```

- Use `float64` for `field.ValueNumber`, `bool` for `field.ValueBoolean`, and keep `store.Value` for `field.ValueJSON`.
- Type `.AfterRead` transforms on virtual fields the same way, such as `operation.Change[string]`.
- `field.OutputField` is now `field.VirtualField[T]`, and `field.AsOutput(node)` is now `field.AsVirtual[T](node)`.
- A virtual field declared with a `nil` resolver needs its type written out, as in `field.Virtual[string]("label", nil)`.

## Data and deployment compatibility

The schema manifest, generated contracts, REST/SDK wire formats and stored data are unchanged: a virtual field declares the same value type as before. This release needs no database migration.
